candidate.answerReason: Equal tangent lengths convert the perimeter into AB+AC=40. The triangle inequality confirms that Q lies on segment PR.

methods.label: Replace the third side using equal tangents
methods.explanation:
Tangent segments from the same exterior point have equal lengths. Applying this at \(A\), \(P\), and \(R\) gives
\[
AB=AC=20,\qquad PB=PQ,\qquad RC=RQ.
\]
Because \(P\) and \(R\) lie on the stated segments, \(PB=20-AP\) and \(RC=20-AR\).

We also need to establish that \(Q\) lies on segment \(PR\). If it lay outside that segment, collinearity would give
\[
\begin{aligned}
PR&=|PQ-RQ|\\
&=|(20-AP)-(20-AR)|\\
&=|AR-AP|.
\end{aligned}
\]
This contradicts the triangle inequality \(|AR-AP|<PR\) in triangle \(APR\). Therefore \(Q\) lies on segment \(PR\), so \(PR=PQ+QR\).

The perimeter is consequently
\[
\begin{aligned}
AP+AR+PR
&=AP+AR+PQ+QR\\
&=(AP+PB)+(AR+RC)\\
&=AB+AC=40.
\end{aligned}
\]
The answer is \(\mathrm{C}\).
